clue.text: Refuse to list cases

definitions.meaning: to turn down or say no to something
in grammar, to recite the case forms of a noun, as Latin students do

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to hand over a list of cases.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: turning down an offer, and reciting the grammatical cases of a noun in order.

clue.text: Visits to ensure eye medication has been administered

parts.note: eye drops are a common liquid eye treatment
once given, the medicine is in, that is applied

explanation.surface: A nurse calls round to make sure the patient's eye drops were given.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop in is to pay a casual visit, so the phrasal verb matches visits.

clue.text: Otherwise retain actresses unlikely to wrinkle

indicators.note: otherwise means in another way, so the letters are arranged differently

explanation.surface: Ageing actresses are kept on because they never seem to wrinkle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Otherwise' rearranges the fifteen letters of RETAIN ACTRESSES.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric treated to resist creasing keeps smooth, so it does not easily wrinkle.

clue.text: Register popular archdeacon of right-wing views

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon
a Tory is a member of Britain's right-of-centre Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A popular churchman with conservative views is enrolled.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory is a register or detailed list of goods held.

clue.text: Noblemen lodging money with auditors

indicators.note: the word for auditors gives lodging to, or contains, the money letter

parts.note: auditors are listeners, so ears are what audit
L, from Latin librae, stands for pounds sterling

explanation.surface: Aristocrats deposit their funds with accountants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditors' misleads towards accountants; here they are listeners, hence EARS.
explanation.definitionFit: Earls are British peers, a rank of nobleman.

clue.text: Articles about fortified wines

parts.note: re is the Latin-derived word for about or concerning
port is a fortified wine from Portugal, here in the plural

explanation.surface: A magazine runs pieces on sherries and ports.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspaper articles are reports of events, so the two words are synonyms here.

clue.text: Listen to Sarah again before the premiere

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again
to hear is to listen to
Sal is a familiar short form of the name Sarah

explanation.surface: A director tells the cast to hear Sarah once more before opening night.
explanation.definitionFit: A rehearsal is the practice run held before a show's first performance, so it is what comes before the premiere.

clue.text: Utterly quiet for a bit

indicators.note: read as uttered, this signals that a word for quiet is spoken out loud

parts.note: peace is quiet or calm

explanation.surface: Someone asks for complete silence for a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Utterly' looks like 'completely' but means 'as uttered', so PEACE becomes a word said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a bit or portion of something.

clue.text: Monarch and General Mitcham are moved by military music

parts.note: R, for rex or regina, stands for a monarch

indicators.note: moved letters are shifted about into a new order

explanation.surface: The King and a general are stirred by a band's martial tune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are moved' rearranges R with GENERAL MITCHAM; Mitcham is a district in south London.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimental march is the tune adopted by a regiment for parades, a type of military music.

clue.text: Can enter Jerusalem to act as observer

indicators.note: the word for can goes into the word for Jerusalem

parts.note: Sion, or Zion, is a biblical name for Jerusalem
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A container is brought into the Holy City for an observer.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit in on a meeting is to attend as an observer rather than a participant.

clue.text: 12½% had a drink too many

definitions.meaning: an eighth, that is one divided by eight, written as a fraction
slightly drunk, an old British idiom

explanation.surface: A figure of twelve and a half per cent sits beside a tipsy reveller.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for being a little drunk literally describes the fraction one-eighth, which is twelve and a half per cent.

clue.text: Woman from America in school sickbay

indicators.note: the letters for America are placed inside the word for the sickbay

parts.note: san is short for sanatorium, a British boarding-school sickbay
US is the abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A woman from the States ends up in the school sanatorium.
explanation.definitionFit: Susan is a woman's name, so a woman is a fair, if broad, definition by example.

clue.text: Declares chap to be a renowned politician

parts.note: to declare is to state, here in the third person
a chap is a man, in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a man is a famous politician.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is a respected, experienced political leader, a synonym for an eminent politician.

clue.text: Corrupt Corsican takes time to deliver drugs

indicators.note: the scrambled word takes in, or contains, the letter for time
corrupt suggests something debased or altered, so the letters of the next word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A crooked islander from Corsica is a drug dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corrupt' rearranges CORSICAN to NARCOICS, and 'takes' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics are drugs, especially illegal ones such as opiates.

clue.text: Usually at home wearing a brass hat

parts.note: being in means being at home
brass hat is slang for a senior officer such as a general, from the gold braid on the cap

explanation.surface: An officer lounges at home in his braided cap.
explanation.definitionFit: In general means usually or as a rule, an everyday idiom.

clue.text: Border added to new material

parts.note: a line marks a border or boundary

explanation.surface: A dressmaker sews a border onto fresh fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Linen is a fabric woven from flax, so it is a kind of material.

clue.text: Tall, energetic redhead of advanced years

parts.note: long and tall both mean of great height or length
live, as in a live wire, means energetic
the head of red is its first letter

explanation.surface: A tall, lively ginger-haired person is getting on in years.
explanation.definitionFit: A long liver is someone who lives to a great age, so the phrase describes a person of advanced years.

clue.text: Irritable instruction to evaluate algebraic unknown

parts.note: test, as an imperative, tells you to evaluate something
x, y and z are the usual unknowns in algebra

explanation.surface: A grumpy maths teacher tells the class to find the value of a variable.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy is a synonym for irritable or short-tempered.

clue.text: Vehicle for Jack to carry army doctors

indicators.note: the sailor word carries, or holds, the letters for the army doctors

parts.note: a jack tar, or tar, is a sailor
RAMC is the Royal Army Medical Corps, the British Army's medical service

explanation.surface: A sailor needs transport to bring military medics along.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramcar is a passenger vehicle running on rails along streets.

clue.text: Old spice offered by windswept girl

parts.note: gal is an informal word for a girl
something windswept is out in a gale, read as the two words in and gale

explanation.surface: A girl blown about by the wind offers an old-fashioned spice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Windswept' is read as 'in gale', supplying IN and GALE after GAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Galingale is an aromatic root of the ginger family, used as a spice in medieval cookery.

clue.text: Determined that each service is in French

parts.note: RN, the Royal Navy, is one of the armed services
est is French for is

explanation.surface: Each service in France is described as resolute.
explanation.definitionFit: Earnest means serious and resolute, close to determined.

clue.text: A second-rate dyer who refuses to vote

parts.note: B is the grade for second-class or second-rate
a stainer colours wood or fabric, as a dyer does

explanation.surface: A mediocre dyer declines to cast a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: An abstainer is someone who formally declines to cast a vote, matching one who refuses to vote.

clue.text: Current fashion in London

parts.note: AC is alternating current
ton is an old word for fashion or high style

explanation.surface: The latest fashion is all the rage in London.
explanation.walkthrough: ACTON is a district of west London; the definition names it by its city.
explanation.definitionFit: Acton is a suburb in the west of London, so the clue defines it by location.

clue.text: Chain for the stove

definitions.meaning: a line of mountains or hills
a cooking stove, as in a kitchen cooker

explanation.surface: A chain is fixed to the cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a mountain chain and a kitchen cooking stove.

clue.text: Primate depicted in remarkable mural at church

indicators.note: the answer is pictured inside the words that follow, running across them

explanation.surface: A monkey-like creature is painted in a striking mural at a church.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'remarkabLE MURal'; 'at church' only finishes the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A lemur is a primate native to Madagascar, so the general term defines it.

clue.text: Canons served an order to give precise reference

parts.note: a cathedral chapter is the body of its canons

indicators.note: putting in order means rearranging, so the letters of served an are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Church canons serve a formal order demanding an exact citation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' rearranges SERVED AN into AND VERSE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means an exact citation, originally of a passage in the Bible.

clue.text: Somehow I learnt that it pertains to ocular membrane

indicators.note: somehow implies the letters arrive by some unstated rearrangement

explanation.surface: A student has somehow learnt a fact about the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes anything relating to the retina, the light-sensitive membrane at the back of the eye.

clue.text: One's clearly being discussed within audible range

definitions.note: the distance within which a sound can be heard

parts.note: read as one's own organs of hearing, the parts said to burn when a person is gossiped about
by folk belief the ears of someone talked about grow hot, so the phrase supplies that word

explanation.surface: Someone is plainly the topic of gossip within hearing distance.
explanation.walkthrough: Folk belief says your ears burn when others talk about you, so the subject's ears are hot; 'within' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Earshot is the distance within which a sound can be heard, a synonym for hearing range.
